en.title: Count Pairs That Match with One Digit Swap
en.description:
For each i<j, the pair is valid if the decimal representation of numbers[j] can become numbers[i] with at most one swap (swapping one pair of positions); no swap is also allowed. Only numbers with the same number of digits are counted. Find the number of pairs. A swap must not create a leading zero.

The input protocol and the examples in this batch were compiled by CSWork.
en.input: The first line contains n (1..100000), and the second line contains n integers (0..10^9) in ordinary decimal representation.
en.output: Output the number of valid pairs; the result may exceed 32 bits.
en.explanation: Process according to the definite rules above; see the accompanying editorial for the approach, proof of correctness, and complexity.
hints: Process from left to right. Enumerate the valid representations the current number can form with no swap or by swapping any pair of different positions, and accumulate using prefix frequencies.
